answer: The graph explorer draws from the `relation` index, which was introduced in Edge > 2.9.0 (per the CHANGELOG entry that added the new relation indexed object and the experimental Object Graph, now called Graph View).

--- Graph View.md ---
Opening the graph
An interactive object-graph explorer visualizes [[Object|objects]] (pages, items, blocks) and the typed [[Tag/relation|relations]] between them — letting you navigate your space by structure rather than by name.

--- Reference/Technical Reference.md ---
External interfaces | Indexing
* [[Reference/Indexing Internals]] — index structure and behavior.

--- Object Graph.md ---
Object Graph
This page is now [[Graph View]].

--- CHANGELOG.md ---
CHANGELOG | Edge > 2.9.0
* New [[Tag/relation|relation]] indexed object capturing generalized object-to-object relationships. This is a successor to `link`, which still exists as a virtual collection built on top of `relation`.
* New experimental [[Object Graph]]: an interactive, force-directed graph explorer over the [[Tag/relation|relation]] index. Try it via ${widgets.commandButton("Graph: Explore")} and ${widgets.commandButton("Graph: Global Page Map")}.
* Picker fuzzy search: replaced Fuse.js with a custom scorer that supports multi-token queries, path-aware ranking, and some typo tolerance.
* UX: a _lot_ of little visual tweaks and usability fixes all over the place that hopefully will trigger less of your OCD, including:
  * On narrow viewports (<800px) header `#` markers no longer get pushed off-screen when the cursor enters a heading
  * Positioning of the page title is now (more) left-aligned with editor text.

--- ADR/003 Indexed Object Graph.md ---
Context | Decision
Continuously maintain an **[[Object Index]]**: a structured, queryable graph automatically extracted from the markdown. Every meaningful element — [[Tag/page|pages]], headers, [[Tag/task|tasks]], list items, [[Tag|tags]], links — becomes an **[[Object|object]]** (a “row”) with attributes, typed by one or more tags (“tables”), queried via [[Space Lua/Integrated Query]] and the [[API/index]] API.

Two principles hold it together:

* **Markdown is the source of truth.** Every indexed object has a representation in the markdown. The index is derived, can be flushed, and rebuilt from the files at any time (`Space: Reindex`). It is a cache, not the canonical store.
* **The index lives in the client.** It is built into IndexedDB in the browser ([[ADR/007 Core Application Logic on the Client]], [[ADR/001 Offline-First PWA]]) and maintained incrementally.
